persona: Ivy Nakamura, 10, 4th grader in Shoreline, WA. Plays defender on a U10 rec team called the Purple Lightning, started soccer last year, still mixed up about offside, plays games on her mom's iPad and her dad's phone.
first_week:
Monday: Dad showed me because it's his soccer thing. The arcade machine looks SO cool, like the one at the pizza place after games. Then the board came up with 18 hexagons, all with words on them, and I didn't know most of them. Rangers FC? Borussia something? I tapped a white one that said "throw-in" because I know what a throw-in is. I got it right and a little black pentagon went into my ball. That felt good. Then I tapped another white one, and it was about some English team winning a title in some year. I guessed. Wrong. Game over. That took like one minute. I said "that's IT?" and Dad laughed, which made it worse.
Tuesday: I learned white doesn't mean easy for ME. It means easy for Dad. I looked for words I knew. Found "bussin" (the Kid Slang one) and got it, and a red card one about how many players are on a team, which was weird because that one was easy. Got 4 chips, then a Liga MX one I had to guess and missed it. Nil. Four right and it still says Nil? That felt unfair.
Wednesday: Dad and I played together on the couch, me picking and him reading. We argued about which tiles to pick, and that was the best part. We got a Goal. I made him text Grandma from his phone: "Triviela, ⚽ Goal." Grandma sent a heart.
Thursday: practice, forgot.
Friday: played alone on the iPad. Missed the second card. Nil. Closed it and watched YouTube.
Saturday: our coach said "offside" at my game and I remembered a card that explained it. That was actually cool.
Sunday: I asked Dad if he'd done it yet. So I guess I'll keep playing, but only with him, or if there's more stuff a kid like me knows.
play_daily: Maybe. Yes if Dad plays it with me or against me, because beating Dad is the whole point. No if most days I'm out after one or two cards on teams I've never heard of. Getting Nil three days in a row would make me stop by week two.
share: I don't have a phone, so I'd make Mom or Dad text it. Mostly to Grandma, and to my friend Harper's mom so Harper can see. I'd only share Goal or better. I'd NEVER share Nil, especially Nil after 5 right, that's embarrassing and wrong. The soccer ball emojis are good, I can read that fast. A grid of squares wouldn't mean anything to me or Grandma. I'd share more if it showed how close I got, and if Harper played too so we could compare.
love: The arcade machine look. It feels like a real game, not homework
Picking any tile I want. I feel smart when I find one I know
Watching the pentagons go into my ball, and the ball filling up
The sentence fills in with the answer and tells me what it means. I learned what offside is that way
Kid Slang cards, because I know those and Dad doesn't

Hook words I can't read or say, like long German and Spanish team names
Being out after one card. Two minutes and it's done and I feel dumb
Getting 5 right and it still saying Nil like I got zero

later: Picture cards on a glowing field: is she offside, what's this line on the field. Looking is easier than reading for me
The anonymous counter so the colors fix themselves when lots of kids miss a 'white' one

Leaderboards. I'd be at the bottom of the whole world

The 6x6 grid in the share text. Nobody I text would understand it
Hints, extra lives or a practice mode. I'd want them, but then it's just a different game, and Dad says the one-miss thing is what makes it exciting
Instructions screens. I figured it out by tapping, that's fine

persona: Tessa Nakamura, 13, eighth grader in Ballard, outside back on a U14 girls' club team in Seattle, Reign fan, two-hour Screen Time limit she fights with her mom about daily.

I do all the white tiles first like a coward, get 6, ball fills, GOAL. That felt actually good. Then I stare at the yellows for a while and stop because I don't want to look dumb. Post "⚽ Goal". Wednesday: the board is like half names I've never heard of. Pachuca, Lens, Atalanta, some Bundesliga guy. It feels like my dad's quiz. I miss on a medium about Liga MX and get Nil and kind of don't care. Thursday: there's a slang card. "The halftime orange slices were ____" and the answer is bussin. Nobody says bussin anymore. I screenshot it to the chat with "who wrote this 😭" and everyone roasts it. Honestly that was the most talked-about card all week, but not in a good way. Friday: I forget until Maddie posts "⚽⚽ Brace" at lunch. I play in the bathroom so I can catch up. Get a Goal, try one red about the 8-second keeper rule because I literally play and know that, get it, then miss a yellow. Still Goal. play_daily: Maybe, honestly leaning yes for a few weeks, but only because my team chat would be doing it. If nobody posts first, I forget. share: Yes, to my team group chat every day I get at least a Goal, and to my dad because he'd be competitive about it. Not on my Insta story, that's too much. Nil I'd only post if somebody else already posted Nil, or as a joke. "⚽⚽ Brace" alone is kind of boring though. I'd share way more if it showed I took red cards, like one row of the tiles I picked in order (⬜⬜🟨🟥⬜❌). Then a Brace with two reds beats a Brace with all whites and we can argue about it. love: Picking my own tiles. Taking the white ones to bank a Goal and then deciding whether to risk a red is the actual game, and that's what my team argued about in the tent
White, yellow and red card colors for difficulty. I got it instantly with zero explaining, it's soccer
The ball filling up with black pentagons, and the GOAL moment at 6. That needs to feel big
Everybody gets the same board, so we can compare in the chat and blame the same hard card

Sound that plays automatically. I play in class and in the bathroom

Fast on a phone in iMessage, with a good link preview when someone posts it in the chat

Picture cards, offside first. My team argues about offside every game and I'd love settling it
The anonymous counter so tiles that are 'easy' but everyone misses get moved up

Endless mode, practice mode, or replaying today. If I can retry, the Goal means nothing
Hints, jokers, lifelines, a second chance
A tutorial or 'Great job!' popups
Avatars, outfits, mascots, badges

I take the white tiles first. Most are stuff I know from playing (throw-ins, how many subs). One easy was about NWSL and I guessed. Got 8 right, Goal, then missed a hard Liga MX one. play_daily: Maybe, leaning yes, but only if my friends play. Alone I'd quit by day 4, there's nothing pulling me back except beating someone. It's fast, it's soccer, and one miss ends it so it never wastes my time, that part is good. If the team chat dies, I die with it.
share: Yes, to the team group chat and to one friend I'm beefing with, not to my parents (my dad would find out from Jonah's dad anyway). I'd share Goal or better. Picking my own tiles. Going for a red card first is a power move and everyone can see you did it
Card colors for difficulty (white/yellow/red) make sense instantly, I didn't need it explained
Everyone has the same board, so in the hotel we could yell about the same question

persona: Jess Kowalczyk, 35, payroll manager in Chicago, two kids (9 and 6), left back for the Old Style Ladies in a Sunday women's 30+ rec league, casual Arsenal fan since a semester in London, 24 minutes each way on the Blue Line.
first_week: Monday: Bri, our keeper, drops the link in the team WhatsApp with "⚽ Goal, the red ones are mean." I open it at Damen. The cabinet looks cute, and I get what's going on in about three seconds: tiles, colors, tap one. I go whites first, obviously. Five whites go fine, then I tap a white Liga MX one, guess wrong, and I'm done on 5. One short of a goal. I'm annoyed, and I'm annoyed in the good way. I read the means line and think, ok, fair. Tuesday: smarter. I skip any white whose hook I don't recognize and grab the yellow 'Arsenal' tile because I lived through that title. Bank a goal by Division. Miss a red Bundesliga one at 8. Text the chat "⚽ Goal, Arsenal tile was a gift." Wednesday: lose signal in the tunnel mid-run. If it reset me I'd be furious, and that's the day I'd quit. Thursday: a Kid Slang card. I don't know what 'mid' means in that sentence, ask my 9-year-old at dinner, and she's thrilled to know something I don't. Best part of the week, honestly. Friday: Brace for the first time, 13 right. I screenshot nothing, I just paste the text into the team chat and my husband's. Saturday I forget. Sunday after our match, four of us play it at the bar table and compare which tiles we picked. That conversation is the game for me. By the end of the week the real puzzle isn't white vs red, it's 'which of these do I actually know?' A red Arsenal tile is easier for me than a white Liga MX one, and reading the hooks for that is the fun.
play_daily: Maybe, leaning yes on weekdays. It fits my train ride exactly, it ends cleanly, and losing on one miss gives me a reason to come back tomorrow. But I'll keep coming back only if my team chat keeps playing. If I'm the only one, I drift off by week three. Weekends I'll skip, and I don't want to be punished for that.
share: Yes, to the Old Style Ladies WhatsApp (11 women) and to my husband, who will pretend he isn't competitive. Brace and Hat trick are great words to send. I'd even send Nil with a skull if it was a funny day. More likely to share: one tap copies it, and it's short enough not to clog the chat. A tiny grid would actually help me, not because of colors but because the bar argument is 'you went for the reds first?' If it's a 6 × 6 wall of emoji, though, I'm cutting it before I paste. Less likely to share: if it pastes a long URL, adds hashtags, or says anything braggy for me.
love: It ends. Five minutes, done, no endless mode pulling me back in
One miss and out: it stings in a way that makes me want tomorrow
The hooks. Seeing 'Arsenal' or 'Rabona' on a tile and thinking 'that's mine' is the real choice
Learning one real thing even on a bad day, especially rules stuff I can use Sunday
Women's game sitting right next to the men's like it's normal, which it should be

No accounts, no ads, no timer

Long sentences. If I have to read a card twice, it's too long
Streak counters or guilt notifications. I have two kids, I'm missing Saturdays

persona: Danny Reyes, 35, HVAC estimator in Oakland, two kids (7 and 4), center back with a dodgy left knee for an over-30s Sunday league side called Lake Merritt Athletic, half-supports Spurs because of a college roommate, rides BART 22 minutes each way.
first_week:
Monday: Teo, our left back, drops the link in the team WhatsApp with "⚽ Goal, the reds are evil." I open it on BART. Honeycomb of tiles, white, yellow, red, little words on them. Nobody told me one miss kills the day, so I tap a red "Rabona" tile first just to see what happens. Get it right, a pentagon drops into the middle. Cool. Tap a yellow "Liga MX" one, guess, wrong, done. I didn't know that was it. Felt cheated, not because of the rule but because I didn't know the rule before I gambled. Nil. Didn't share.

Tuesday: now I get it. I clear all six whites first, it's like warming up before a match. Goal. The means line on the keeper eight-second thing is genuinely useful, I bring it up Sunday when our keeper dawdles. I text "⚽ Goal" to the WhatsApp. Teo replies with a Brace. Now it's on.

Wednesday: whites, then I eye the yellows. I take the EPL and rules ones, skip the Ligue 1 and NWSL ones. Get to 11 and miss a Bundesliga yellow I should've left alone. One chip short of a Brace. That stings in a good way, it was my call. Thursday I'm late, play it on the platform waiting, get interrupted by my 4-year-old's daycare calling, come back an hour later and need it to be exactly where I left it. Friday: a Kid Slang card, "bussin," I actually ask my 7-year-old at dinner the night before a different one comes up and laugh about it. Saturday I skip it, kids' games all morning. Sunday after our match the guys are comparing in the parking lot. That's the moment I know it's sticking: it became a thing between us, not a thing on my phone.
play_daily: Maybe leaning yes. It fits the train exactly if a run is under five minutes and it never makes me wait on animations. What keeps me is the Wednesday feeling: losing because I chose the wrong tile, not because the game sprang a coin-flip on me. If red cards turn out to be Liga MX trivia only a Liga MX fan could know, I'll start banking whites and quitting, and that gets boring in two weeks. If the reds are hard-but-gettable stuff a real fan knows, and the means lines keep teaching me things I can use on Sunday, I'm in. I'll skip weekends sometimes, so no guilt mechanics please.
share: Yes, to the Lake Merritt Athletic WhatsApp (14 guys, about 5 would play daily) and to my brother Rob, an Arsenal fan, mostly to needle him. The bare "⚽⚽ Brace" works for a week, then it's just a number. What would make me share more: one line showing the colors I took in order, like ⬜⬜⬜🟨🟥🟨... with the miss marked. That line IS the story ("you went red on card two, you maniac"). Not a 6 by 6 grid, that's noise and nobody reads it in a group chat. Would make me share less: a long link, a URL with tracking junk, emoji spam, or anything that brags for me ("I'm a genius!"). I'd share a Nil too if I died on the first red, that's funny.
love: Choosing my own risk. White, yellow, red as card colors is instantly readable to anyone who's played, no legend needed
Goals are banked. A miss never erases what I earned, so I'm willing to be brave late
The means line. A rule fact I can drop on the ref or my keeper on Sunday is worth more to me than any score
It's a soccer ball, not another guess-the-European-striker game for the Athletic-subscriber crowd. My kid's coach could play it, my brother could play it
Brace and Hat trick as the result names. That's how we actually talk
No accounts, no ads. I'd bounce from a sign-up wall on the train
turn_offs: Not knowing on day one that one miss ends it. Zero instructions is fine for most things, but the stakes have to be clear before I make my first gamble, or the first loss feels like a trick

Hard cards that are pure coin flips (a Liga MX club's founding year, a Ligue 1 stat). Hard should mean a real fan knows it, as the brief says. If it drifts into trivia-nerd territory I stop touching reds
Stale current facts. If it tells me a manager who got sacked last month is still in charge, I stop trusting every card
Anything slow: tile flips, chip-flying animations I have to sit through, marquee flicker every time I open it. Cute once, annoying on day 4
Losing my run because BART went underground or I switched apps
More than one Kid Slang card a day. One is a laugh. Three and it's a dad joke game
Tiny tap targets on 18 hexes. I'm one-thumbing this standing up, holding a rail
must_have_v1: The board and the loop: 18 tiles with hook word plus white/yellow/red, tap any, chip into the ball, 6 chips = goal, one miss ends the day. Big enough hexes to hit one-thumbed on a moving train, fits with no scrolling

One unmistakable first-run cue that a miss ends the day and 6 is a goal (the center ball showing 6 empty chip slots does half of it, one short line the first time does the rest). Once, then never again
The day locks and resumes: close the app, lose signal, come back an hour later, I'm exactly where I was, and I can't replay today. Works offline once loaded
The means line after every answer, right or wrong
A one-tap copy of the share text: number, result, and one row of colored squares in the order I took them with the miss marked
later: After the day ends, let me tap the untouched tiles to see their answers and means lines, unscored. When I die on card 4 with 15 minutes of train left, I want to learn the rest
Picture cards, especially offside and ref signals. That's the stuff we argue about every Sunday and I'd love it
A plain streak number and a countdown to tomorrow's board

Dark mode for the late train home

Leaderboards, accounts, friends lists, profiles. The group chat is the leaderboard
Hints, jokers, second lives, ad-for-a-retry. It kills the Wednesday feeling
Archive or practice mode or endless play. One a day is why I come back
Push notifications or streak-shame. If I skip Saturday for my kids' games, leave me alone
Category filters (no Liga MX for me). The random mix is the fun, and it lets me just skip those tiles anyway

persona: Maureen "Mo" Delaney, 58, retired school librarian in Tacoma, grew up in Kearny NJ, watched Rossi in '82 with her Scottish dad, was in the Rose Bowl in '99, Sounders season ticket holder since 2009, grandmother to Ellie (10, plays U11 in Puyallup)
first_week: Monday my son drops the link in the family chat with "Mom this is your game." First thing I do is hold the phone further away. Pixel font, green on black, I'm squinting, and if I need my readers for every tile I'll still play but I'll grumble. The board is gorgeous. I get the white/yellow/red cards in one second, no explanation needed, that's the best idea in the whole thing. I tap whites first like a sensible woman, bank a Goal, feel brave, tap a red tile that says "Leverkusen" and it's about a current manager. Gone. One Goal. I'm annoyed at myself, which is the right kind of annoyed. I text my sister Fran in Jersey: "Goal. Got greedy." Tuesday I hunt for hooks from my era. I see "Pelé" on a red and grab it early while my head's clear, and I get it, and that feels wonderful. Wednesday there's a Kid Slang tile that says "rizz." I leave it alone all day, then call Ellie that night to ask what it means. That's honestly my favorite moment of the week and it happened off the screen. Thursday I miss the very first card I tap. Nil, done in 30 seconds. I'm cross, but I respect it, and I'm back Friday. Friday I get a Brace and Fran only got a Goal, and I'm insufferable in the group text. Saturday I miss a card I'm sure is wrong about the '94 World Cup. If the means line had confirmed I was wrong with a real fact, fine. If I'd found an error I'd have stopped trusting the whole thing. Sunday I get to 17 and miss the last yellow. Seventeen right and my text says the same "Brace" as twelve. That stung more than the miss.
play_daily: Yes, if I can read it without my glasses and it takes under five minutes. What brings me back isn't the game, it's Fran. We've done Wordle together since 2022. If Triviela gives us a new thing to needle each other about, it goes into the morning coffee rotation. If the hard tiles are all this season's Bundesliga managers and La Liga transfer fees, I'll drift away by week three, because then it's a game for my son, not me.
share: Yes, every day, to Fran first, then the family chat when I beat my son. The plain three lines are right, I don't want a big grid, I'm not decoding a honeycomb in emoji. But I need my count. "Brace" for 12 and for 17 is not the same day, and 17 is a story I want to tell. Something like "⚽⚽ Brace · 17" is all it needs. What would make me less likely: anything that looks like an ad, a long link, or the result spoiling a card for Fran before she plays. What would make me more likely: seeing which color I died on, one emoji, like a 🟥 at the end. That tells Fran I went down swinging at a red, not a white.
love: The white, yellow, red card colors for difficulty. I understood it instantly and it makes every tap a decision. That's the game.
Picking my own tiles. I can go after the Pelé and Mia Hamm cards while my head is fresh and leave the Gen Alpha slang for last, or never.
One miss ends it. Short, clean, honest. I don't want to play for twenty minutes.
The means line. I'm a librarian. Learning one real fact a day, even on a miss, is why I'd tell my friends about it.
The women's game in there as a full citizen, not a side category. I was at the Rose Bowl. Give me Brandi Chastain cards.
Kid Slang as the one oddball, because it sends me to my granddaughter. Keep it to just that one.
The ball filling with black pentagons. That's lovely and I don't need it explained.
turn_offs: Text I can't read. Pixel fonts at small sizes on a glowing screen are hard on 58-year-old eyes. If the hook words on 18 little hexagons are tiny, the whole board fails for me.
A wrong fact. One wrong card about a World Cup I watched and I'm out for good. Official sources are right, but someone needs to sanity-check the old history too.
Hard meaning current. If every red tile is this season's men's European club trivia, the game punishes people like me for having watched longer.
Same result word for 12 and 17 right.
A timer. Never. I'm drinking coffee.
Nagging. No notifications, no streak guilt, no 'don't break your streak!' pop-ups.
Cute arcade jank getting in the way. The cabinet is charming, but if I have to wait through a sign flickering every morning, it gets old by Wednesday.
must_have_v1: Readable text on the board and the card at phone size, for older eyes. Bigger hook words beat a prettier honeycomb. Test it on someone over 55.
The board as described: all 18 tiles, hook word plus white/yellow/red color, tap in any order, one miss ends it, the ball filling in the middle.
The means line after every answer, right or wrong, so a miss still teaches me something.
Share text with the number right, not just the result word: 'Triviela #42 / ⚽⚽ Brace · 17 / triviela.net'. Copy to clipboard in one tap.
Cards that are actually right, with the history and women's game carrying weight in the hard tier, so a long-time fan has an edge, not just someone who reads this week's transfer news.
later: Picture cards on the chalkboard pitch, especially offside and ref signals. I'd love those, and they'd be great for Ellie too. But only once the basic board is solid.
The Soccer 101 basics category, so Ellie can play alongside me and win some tiles I'd think are beneath me.
A quiet record of my own days played and best score, on my phone only, no streak pressure.
The anonymous counter that re-sorts card difficulty from real results. Smart, invisible, do it once there are players.
A tiny marker in the share for the color I went out on.
dont_build: Accounts, leaderboards, friends lists. Fran and I have a group text, that's our leaderboard.
Push notifications or streak nagging.
A big emoji grid in the share. Three lines and a number is enough.
Timers or speed bonuses.
Hints, jokers, second chances, or a practice mode. The stakes are the point.
More non-soccer categories. Kid Slang works because it's one wink. Five of them and it's a different game.
Dark mode. The screen is already black. Spend that time on font size.
Long intro animations or attract screens every morning.

persona: Walt Brennan, 58, retired IBEW electrician in Burien, WA. Went to NASL Sounders games at the Kingdome as a kid, watched Spain '82 on a Spanish-language channel with rabbit ears, and his granddaughter Maddie, 11, plays U12 rec in Des Moines.
first_week:
Monday my son texts me a link: "Dad, this is your kind of thing." I open it with my coffee at 6:40. The cabinet makes me grin. It looks like the Galaga machine at the bowling alley on Ambaum. Then I squint. Eighteen little hexagons, green pixel words, and I'm holding the phone at arm's length. I find "Rossi" on a white tile and "Rabona" on a red one and I'm in heaven. I pick the safe whites first because I'm not an idiot, get six, and the ball fills up. That's a goal, and I feel it. Then I get greedy on a yellow that says "Bundesliga" and pick wrong. Done. The answer fills in with a little explanation, and fine, I didn't know who won the Bundesliga last year. I'm sore but I get it. One goal. I text my son "⚽ Goal," and he sends back "Brace, old man." Now it's on.
Tuesday I go straight for the reds that look old-school, "Azteca," "Cruyff," and clear four. Then a white tile reads "bussin" and I'm cooked, to use the word. Nil. Honestly that stings more than the Bundesliga did, because it was a white tile and I lost the whole day to my granddaughter's vocabulary. But I text Maddie a screenshot and ask what bussin means, and she sends me eleven laughing faces. Best text I got all week. So I'm torn.
Wednesday and Thursday I've learned to read the board. Old names and rules first, current MLS and NWSL rosters last or never. Brace on Thursday. I text it to my son and to the old Sunday league group chat, five guys over 55 who still argue about Italia '90.
Friday I fat-finger a red tile when I meant the white one next to it. Miss. Day over. I put the phone down annoyed, and that's the closest I came to quitting.
Saturday Maddie's game is at 9, so I play in the car after. Sunday I get a Hat trick, all eighteen, and I'd frame it if I could. By Sunday it's part of the morning, like the crossword used to be.
play_daily: Yes. One run, it's quick, the stakes are real, and it's the same board my son gets, so there's a fight every morning. The one thing that would make it a maybe: if the hard cards lean on this season's managers and transfer news. My edge is history, rules and the World Cup. If the hopper starves that, I'm just guessing at stuff I don't follow and I'll drift off within a month.
share: Yes, every day I score, and on Nil days too if my son beat me, because I'll want to say something. Three places: my son (the rivalry), the Sunday league group chat (the bragging), and Maddie now and then. Keep the three lines. "Brace" and "Hat trick" do all the work, and the guys love that it uses real soccer words. A grid would make me less likely: six lines of colored dots in a group chat of 58-year-olds is clutter, and I'd have to explain it. The puzzle number matters more than you think. It's how my son and I know we played the same board.
love: Real soccer words for the results: Nil, Goal, Brace, Hat trick. Any fan reads that in one second.
Picking the tiles myself. Reading the board and deciding when to get brave is the actual game, and it rewards someone who knows what he knows.
Goals are banked. Losing on tile 14 still leaves me with my Brace, so I'm never punished for being greedy late.
The "means" line after a miss. I learned the six-second keeper rule changed, and I told the guys like I'd known it for years.
History and legend cards next to rules cards next to a Scottish club. That mix is the whole charm.
The arcade cabinet look. It's nostalgic for my generation without trying.
turn_offs: Tiny pixel text. Glowing green pixel letters on black at hexagon size are hard on 58-year-old eyes. If I need readers to see the board, I'll stop.
Small hexes that fat fingers can mis-tap. If one accidental tap opens a red card and ends my day, that feels cheap, not hard.

A slang card on a white tile ending my run. It's fair to the kids, but losing the whole day to "bussin" will happen to every grandparent. At least make sure the hook gives it away so I can steer clear.
Hard cards that are really "current season" cards: this year's managers, last week's transfers. That isn't hard, it's homework.
Anything that makes me sign in, nags me for notifications, or shows a streak counter guilting me on days I'm at Maddie's tournament.
must_have_v1: The board with all 18 tiles, white/yellow/red color, readable hooks, and hexes big enough to tap right with a thumb. Do a readability pass with an older person, not just at phone sizes.
Same board for everyone, a puzzle number, one run a day, and a locked "done for today" screen showing my result. No replays.
The three-line share text with the number, ready to paste.
After a miss: the right answer and its "means" line. That's the learning, and it softens the loss.
A fair hopper: hard means a real fan knows it, with history, rules and the World Cup as well represented as this season's news.
later: Picture cards: offside yes or no, name the formation. I'd love those more than anything else on the list, but they can wait.
The anonymous counter that re-sorts difficulty from real results. Quiet, nobody sees it, and it fixes the tags you got wrong.
A text-size option or a large-type mode if the default can't be big enough.
A basics category, so Maddie's teammates' parents can win a Goal on day one.
Dark mode. I don't care, but I know some people do.
dont_build: The 6 × 6 run grid in the share text. Three lines is perfect.
Streaks, badges, stats pages, or a calendar of past results. My group chat is the leaderboard.
Accounts, leaderboards, push notifications. You already said no, so hold the line.
Hints, skips, a second life, "watch an ad to continue." One miss ends it, that's the drama.
An archive or practice mode of past days. It kills the one-a-day feeling.
Instructions screens. But the first tap has to teach me that six right makes a goal, so let the ball filling up do the explaining.

persona: Jess Medeiros, 27, a dental hygienist in Tacoma. She got dragged to a USMNT watch party at a Capitol Hill bar during the 2026 World Cup, went to the Reign home opener this spring, and now has season tickets with two coworkers. She can name half the Reign roster and still says "wait, why was that offside?" every single match.
first_week: Monday: my coworker Kayla texts "Triviela #12 ⚽ Goal" to our Reign group chat with no context. I open it on my lunch break. The cabinet is cute and the board looks like a ball, which I get right away. I don't get the chips yet. I tap a white tile that says "Throw-in" because I know what that is and get it right. A pentagon drops into the middle of the ball and something clicks. I take five more whites, all right, and the ball fills and I get a GOAL. That felt really good. Then I look at what's left: yellows saying "Bundesliga" and "Rangers FC" and a red saying "Rabona". I tap a yellow NWSL one because that's my league and miss it. I'm annoyed, but the means line taught me something and I did score. I text "Goal" back to Kayla. Tuesday: I go straight for whites and miss my third one. Nil. Now the "one miss ends it" rule stings, because I was on the tram for maybe 90 seconds. But the means line was about a rule I'd been wrong about all season, so I screenshot it. Wednesday: I start reading hooks before tapping, which turns out to be the real game. "Golden Boot" sounds safe even as a yellow. I get a Brace and immediately text the group chat AND my brother Marco, who is the one who says "it's not complicated" about offside. Thursday: I take a red early just to see, and it's a Liga MX manager I've never heard of. Instant Nil. That felt like a trick, not a dare. Friday: Goal. Saturday: Nil, but on a card about the World Cup at Lumen Field, which I WAS at, so it hurt in a fun way. Sunday: Brace again, and I'm checking whether Kayla's played yet. By Sunday it's a habit, but only because three of the seven days had a card that taught me something I actually cared about. On the days the board is wall-to-wall men's European clubs, I'd feel like a tourist.
play_daily: Yes, probably, for a month at least. It's two minutes, it has a clean ending, and the white/yellow/red bet is a real decision I make every day. Whether I last past a month depends on two things: whether the board feels like it was made for me some days (NWSL, women's internationals, World Cup 2026, rules I'm fuzzy on) and not just for my brother, and whether a miss on card two leaves me with something, like the means line, instead of just a door slamming.
share: Yes, to the Reign season-ticket group chat (Kayla and Bri) almost every day, and to my brother Marco only on Brace or better, because he's insufferable. "Triviela #42 ⚽⚽ Brace" alone is fine, but kind of flat: it doesn't show I was brave. A single row of colored squares in the order I tapped, like ⬜⬜🟨🟥⬜⬜🟨 ending on the miss, would make me share more, because taking a red early is the brag and the order IS the story. A full 6 × 6 grid is too much, it's a wall of emoji and nobody reads it. I'd share less if the text was cute or wordy, if the link went to an app store or signup, or if Nil looked humiliating. "Nil" is good: it's soccer, it's dry, I'd still send it.
love: The card colors as difficulty. White, yellow, red is instantly readable to anyone who's watched one match, and it turns the board into a bet I make with my own nerve
Chips filling a ball in the middle, and 6 = a goal. When the first goal landed I got it with zero explanation
The means line. Learning a real rule I've been wrong about all season is the reason I'd come back, more than the score
Goals being banked. Missing after a goal still feels like I did something
Hooks that make me guess. Reading 'Golden Boot' and deciding if I trust myself on a yellow is the actual fun
One run and done. I play it on the tram, not in bed for 40 minutes
The arcade look. It's charming and doesn't look like a sports-bro app
Nil / Goal / Brace / Hat trick. I learned 'brace' from this and now I use it at matches
turn_offs: A red card that's a Liga MX assistant coach or a Serie A transfer fee. 'A real fan knows it' has to mean a fan of something I might follow, not just a fan of European men's football
Boards with no women's game on them. If I see zero NWSL, Women's World Cup or women's international cards on a given day, I'd feel the game wasn't for me
Hooks that mean nothing to me ('Rangers FC') on half the board. Then the choice isn't strategy, it's a coin flip
Missing on card two and getting a blank screen and a countdown. I need the means line and a look at the board I didn't get to
Pixel text I have to squint at. The means line especially has to be easy to read, it's the payoff
Kid Slang showing up as a hard red card. 'Bussin' is funny for a parent, but for me it's just a weird card in a soccer game
No way to tell what a chip is on day one. If the rule only clicks after six right answers, someone who misses on card three never gets it
Anything that nags me: streak-loss guilt, notifications, 'Don't break your streak!'
must_have_v1: The 18-tile board with white/yellow/red card colors and hooks that really help me guess. Every tile should be guessable from the hook alone, even if I'm wrong
A balanced daily draw: a cap per category (no more than 2 or 3 from any one league), and at least some women's-game and rules cards every day. Random from the whole pool will produce bad days
The means line on every answer, especially the miss, and after a miss the rest of the board shown so I see what I passed up
The share text with the day number, plus one row of colored squares in the order I tapped. That's it
A center ball that shows 6 empty chip slots from the start, so the goal rule is readable before I earn it, with no text
later: Picture cards, starting with offside only. A glowing chalkboard pitch and 'Onside / Offside / Not involved' is the single thing that would make me tell people 'this game finally taught me offside'
The anonymous counter that re-sorts difficulty, because your guess at what's hard isn't my reality, and the colors are the whole bet
A basics category, mixed into whites, so beginners always have a safe goal
A tiny streak or history I can look at if I want, never shown as a threat
Dark mode, though the CRT is already mostly black, so it's low priority
dont_build: Accounts, leaderboards, friends lists. The group chat is the leaderboard
A 6 × 6 share grid. One row in tap order says more and fits in a text
Hints, skips, extra lives, a 'free white' power-up. They'd kill the bet
Endless or practice mode. If I can grind, the daily stops mattering
A tutorial screen or instructions overlay. Make the center ball readable instead
More non-soccer categories. Kid Slang is borderline already. Taylor Swift would feel like a different game
Push notifications or streak guilt
Category labels on tiles. The color plus hook is enough, and a 'Bundesliga' badge would just make me skip it

roadmap.step: Write the daily draw rules: 6/6/6 split, a per-category cap, a minimum of women's-game and rules cards, a same seed worldwide
roadmap.why: Pure random will hand someone like me a board of German and Scottish men's clubs, and I'd quit on that day

roadmap.step: Audit hooks and hard-tier cards for 'would a casual fan who follows one club have a shot'
roadmap.why: The hook is the game. A hook I can't read turns strategy into a coin flip, and an obscure red feels like a trick

roadmap.step: Design the end screen: means line, the board you didn't reach, the result word, a copy-share button
roadmap.why: This is where a 30-second Nil turns into learning something and texting it anyway

roadmap.step: Write the share text: day number, result, one row of squares in tap order, the link
roadmap.why: Sharing is the only growth engine you have, and the tap-order row is what makes it a story

roadmap.step: Launch on triviela.net, with Morg approving just enough cards for 60 days of boards

roadmap.why: Offside is the most wanted lesson for people like me. The counter fixes the colors once real people play

verdict: I'd play daily and text it to my Reign group chat, as long as every board has something in it for a newer fan who follows the women's game and every miss teaches me something. Otherwise it's my brother's game and I'm just visiting.

persona: Devin Kowalczyk, 27, physical therapy assistant in Kansas City. Went to a World Cup group game at Arrowhead in June 2026 on a buddy's spare ticket, got hooked, now has a half-season Sporting KC plan with his roommate and watches Arsenal on Saturday mornings because his coworker won't shut up about them. Still nods along when offside comes up.
first_week:
Monday: my buddy Jake drops a link in our group chat, "Fan Shop Guys," with no context. I open it on my lunch break. The cabinet thing makes me smile. Then I see the honeycomb and the white, yellow and red tiles and I get it in two seconds, because yellow and red cards are literally the first thing I learned watching the World Cup. Nobody has to explain it. I tap all whites. A throw-in one, a "how many players" one, a Kid Slang one that makes me laugh. Six right, the ball fills, Goal. Then I get greedy and tap a red that says "Ligue 1" and get smoked. Fine. I saw the answer, read the means line, closed it. Took maybe three minutes. I texted the chat "Goal" and Jake had a Brace. Annoying.

Tuesday: I open it before work on purpose. This time I'm actually reading the board, scanning hooks. "Rabona" I know from TikTok. "Rangers FC" I don't really know anything about, but it's yellow, so I skip it. That's the fun part: I'm making a plan. Got 9, died on a yellow about the offside rule. The means line actually taught me something about being level with the second-to-last defender. That's the first time offside has made sense in one sentence.

Wednesday: Nil. Missed a white about Liga MX. A WHITE. I felt a little cheated, because white should mean any World Cup fan gets it, and Liga MX is not that for me. Thought about not coming back.

Thursday: came back anyway because Jake posted Brace again. Got a Brace myself, went all whites and yellows, skipped every red. Felt smart.

Friday and Saturday: I'm in a routine. Open it on the toilet or the bus, three minutes, text the chat. On Saturday I tapped a red first while I was "fresh," hit it, and got a Brace that felt earned.

Sunday: I wanted to know what the other tiles were. I died with 7 tiles untouched and couldn't stop wondering what "Catenaccio" meant. If I can't find out, it bugs me all day.
play_daily: Yes for at least a month, as long as a run stays under 5 minutes and the white tiles feel fair to someone who started watching soccer in 2026. The board choice is what hooks me, because it makes every day feel like my own plan. The thing that would make me drop it is two nil days in a week from white tiles about leagues I've never watched. Then it stops feeling like skill and starts feeling like guessing.
share: Yes, almost every day, to one group chat of three buddies from the Sporting games, and to my coworker who's into Arsenal when I beat him. The base text is good and short. One thing would make me share more: say what color killed me, like "Brace, out on a red." That one extra line tells the story (I was brave, not dumb) and gives Jake something to trash talk. A full 6x6 emoji grid I'd probably skip reading, and it looks like spam in iMessage. I'm less likely to share if the link preview is ugly or broken, or if copying takes more than one tap. I'd share Nil days too if they're funny, but only if the text doesn't make me look like an idiot.
love: The white, yellow and red card colors. Instantly readable to a World Cup convert, and they turn the board into a real gamble
Picking my own path. Grabbing safe whites to bank a goal, then deciding how brave to be, is the whole game for me
The means line. It's the first place offside made sense to me in one sentence, and I'd honestly play just for that
Goals are banked. Missing never takes anything away, so going for a red feels brave, not stupid
Short. Three minutes, one run, done. I don't want more than that from a daily
Odd neighbors, like a trick move next to a Scottish club. It feels like a pub quiz, not homework
The share text is tiny and in soccer language (Brace, Hat trick). Saying 'I got a brace' to my buddies feels cool
turn_offs: White tiles that aren't really easy for a newer fan. A white about Liga MX or a Serie A manager feels like a betrayal of the color
Hook words I can't read at all. If half the board is names I don't know, the choice disappears and it's just colors
Three buttons where I'm purely guessing. A 33% coin flip ending my day doesn't feel like Zach Gage, it feels like a slot machine
Wrong 'current' facts. If a card says a manager is at a club and I know he got sacked, I stop trusting the whole thing
Not being able to see the rest of the board after I die. Leaving 7 tiles a mystery is torture
Tiny pixel text I have to squint at on the bus. The arcade look is cool until I can't read a hook
Anything that feels like it's lecturing me or making me feel dumb for not knowing the Bundesliga
must_have_v1: The same 18-card board for everyone, with a puzzle number and a clear sense of when the next one drops
The honeycomb with readable hooks and the white, yellow and red colors, plus the ball filling so I can see how close I am to a goal
The right answer and its means line after every card, including the one that ends my day
One-tap share that pastes clean into iMessage, ideally with the color I died on
White tiles calibrated for someone who started watching in 2026: rules, basics, World Cup, huge clubs. Save the league-specific stuff for yellow and red
later: After the day ends, let me tap the untouched tiles to read their answers and means lines, no score. It's cheap, it's learning, and it kills the 'what was that one' itch
Picture cards, especially offside on a chalkboard pitch. That's the one thing I'd genuinely want most, because I learn better from a picture than a sentence
The anonymous counter so white, yellow and red sort themselves from real results
A quiet personal record on my phone: days played, best result, how many Hat tricks. No streak shaming
Dark mode, since I play in bed at night
dont_build: Accounts, leaderboards, friends lists. My group chat is the leaderboard
Hints, jokers, second lives, or 'watch an ad to continue'. Banked goals already make losing feel fine
A timer. I play on the bus and get interrupted
An endless or practice mode. Scarcity is why I come back tomorrow
Push notifications or streak guilt
A tutorial or rules screen. The card colors and the filling ball explain it. If people get confused, fix the layout, don't add text
More non-soccer categories. Kid Slang is funny once a day. More than that and it stops being a soccer game
A big emoji grid in the share text. One line about how I went out is plenty
Category labels or extra icons on the tiles. The hook word and the color are enough
